To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) video labeling requires specialized skill, and (2) video annotation can be economically performed on Amazon Mechanical Turk.

1) the cognitive load of a video annotation interface must be minimized, 2) the annotation process must be broken into small tasks that can be completed quickly, 3) a large pool of expert annotators can be identified, and 4) the quality of video annotation can be maximized by leveraging a combination of cloud computing, human computation, and interpolation techniques.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of scalable video labeling systems and the creation of large, high quality, labeled data sets.

two main problems: (1) how to design a video annotation system to minimize the cognitive load on the annotator and maximize the quality of the labels and (2) how to efficiently scale up the annotation process to create massive data sets.
how to economically label video with a large workforce.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best practice for video annotation is to use a combination of human workers and computer algorithms to maximize the quality of annotation while keeping costs low.
we present a framework for economically labeling video data that is orders of magnitude more cost-effective than existing methods.
the most efficient way to annotate video is to have a team of expert annotators, with a good interface, who can use a combination of manual and automated methods, to annotate video.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the ability to economically annotate videos with high quality and that we have developed a framework for doing so.

the most effective way to annotate videos is with a specialized user interface that minimizes the cognitive load on the annotator, and that the best workers are those who have specialized skill in the task.
we have created an efficient and scalable system for video annotation, that can be used for a variety of applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
video annotation is a difficult task that requires a specialized interface, a careful selection of workers, and the use of macro-tasks.
the cost of video annotation scales sub-linearly with respect to the size of the data set.
, despite the common perception that video annotation is difficult and costly, we demonstrate that it is possible to economically scale up video annotation to massive levels.
